newsitem.title: USA: Northeast nuclear plans may be too optimistic.
newsitem.headline: Northeast nuclear plans may be too optimistic.

text.p: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is concerned that plans by Northeast Utilities to restart its idled Millstone nuclear plants by early 1998 might be too optimistic, an NRC spokeswoman said Wednesday.
"We're concerned the restart schedule might be overly optimistic," NRC spokeswoman Diane Screnci told Reuters by telephone.

She was responding to comments by the head of Northeast's nuclear operations on Tuesday that two of the idled Millstone nuclear reactors in Waterford, Conn., would be ready for restart by the end of 1997.
The third Millstone plant will be ready during the first quarter of 1998, said Bruce Kenyon, president and chief executive officer for Northeast's nuclear operations.
Kenyon spoke at a public hearing with NRC officials on the utility's plans to restart its nuclear plants, which have been closed for safety reasons since March of this year.
"There's a lot that needs to be done to bring these units to a state of readiness," Kenyon said.
He said the troubled utility's main challenge was "to fundamentally change how it functions. You need and we need to see an organization that is performing, not promising."
Kenyon did not specify which reactor would be ready first, nor what it would cost Northeast to fix all the design, equipment and management problems.
Tuesday's hearing marked the first time since September, when Kenyon joined the company, that the utility had talked publicly about its restart plans.
Screnci said that some NRC staff members were concerned that there were not enough specifics in Northeast's recovery plan.
"We've now got an extra layer of detail, but at the same time, we recognize that there is a tremendous amount of work that still needs to be done," she said.
"We've also expressed concern about the prospect of a regulatory logjam if all three units are ready to come back up around the same time," said Screnci.
Northeast officials will next outline their restart plans to the federal regulators at a public meeting to be held in Rockville, Maryland on January 30 of next year.
